title: The Uplift Added for Taking the Value Back as Granite Ridge Resort Credit
content:
| What the pass account shows | How the pass record stands on payment | Multiple taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| an amount placed on it to be collected by instalments | the price is still being collected | 1.05, the figure increased by a twentieth |
| no amount placed on it to be collected by instalments | the pass was paid in full at the outset | 1.1, the figure increased by a tenth |
| any other position | any other position | no uplift by this rule |

The schedule above governs the uplift added to the figure coming back as resort credit on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass given up. Where the pass account shows an amount placed on it to be collected by instalments and the price is still being collected, the figure is increased by a twentieth. Where the pass account shows no amount placed on it to be collected by instalments and the pass was paid in full at the outset, it is increased by a tenth. In any other case no uplift is added by this rule.

Note 1. The two cases are alternatives and never hold together: the first rests on an amount having been placed on the pass account to be collected by instalments, the second on no such amount having been placed there at all.

Note 2. An account showing an amount placed on it to be collected by instalments where the price is no longer being collected falls outside both, as does an account showing no such amount where the pass was not paid in full at the outset.

Note 3, worked on hypothetical figures. A figure of 450.60 coming back on a pass account that shows an amount placed on it to be collected by instalments with the price still being collected is increased by a twentieth, giving 473.13. The same figure on a pass account showing no such amount, where the pass was paid in full at the outset, is increased by a tenth, giving 495.66.
